text:
for whatever reason, these interviews are as close as you can get to "markets in practice" versus the other 99% of books which are markets in theory

the only thing I could offer, is that there is a ton of what u could call "pit wisdom" in these older books...as in, trading pit wisdom

like from crusty, grizzled veterans and tape-readers, who are passing along what THEY know from decades in the trading pits, the "open-outcry era" in the photo.

shit that doesn't exist anymore. but markets are very very old, like hundreds of years, the principles are all still valid...ur still trading against a counterparty the same way. its just all digital now.

and so stuff like the PTJ intvw -- he wasn't born knowing those things. the "old masters" of the exchanges and commodity pits taught him, just as they were taught by their mentors.

outside of this intvw-style format, its very hard to find that type of information -- pit wisdom, market pragmatism, "arcana"

frame of reference: compare the obscure shit that Druck knows, vs. the widely-disseminated stuff that Buffett knows

and so without these books, a lot would have been lost to history...major credit is due, esp to Schwager.
